summary: Windows provisioning fails due to duplicate BCD GUID after SSD replacement and disk-clone
description:
Issue summary: Several recently repaired workstations that had SSDs replaced via disk-clone show provisioning failures when attempting to join corporate AAD/Intune during OOBE. Endpoint provisioning stalls at Azure AD join step with error referencing a BCD (Boot Configuration Data) identifier conflict.

Impact: Affected devices cannot complete standard imaging/provision pipeline in lab-staging and must be manually recovered. This blocks ~8 new hires from receiving configured laptops this week and creates extra depot work.

Environment: lab-staging, Windows 11 Enterprise 22H2 base image, provisioning pipeline version: infra/provisioner v3.4.1, region: us-west, affected models: Dell Latitude 7450, Lenovo X1 Carbon Gen 10 (see affected_models field).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Replace SSD and perform sector-level disk-clone from donor image using CloneTool v2.0 with default UUID-preserve option enabled.
2) Boot device to Windows OOBE and connect to corp-net via temporary provisioning VLAN.
3) Provisioning script runs; device reaches "Azure AD Join" step and fails with message "Failed to register device: BCD identifier conflict (GUID already in store)".
4) Manual attempt to run 'bcdedit /export' and inspect BCD store shows duplicate GUID entries matching the donor device.

Observed logs / error snippets:
- Provisioner logs: "[provisioner] AADJoinError: BCD_GUID_CONFLICT: GUID {f2a9b...} already exists in store"
- Windows event log (Setup): "Device registration aborted: BootConfigurationData contains duplicate element"
- Intune MDM logs show device not created due to identifier collision.

Notes: Devices cloned with sector-preserve are showing identical BCD stores and machine-specific boot IDs. The provisioning pipeline expects unique machine/bcd identifiers for Intune device registration and to derive device asset tags used by downstream inventory hooks.
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial report from depot techs — 3 devices in the queue failed AAD join after SSD swap and cloning. Collected bcdedit exports and attached to ticket (attached to internal artifact store).

2026-03-11 Diego Ramos: Reproduced failure in lab. Confirmed cloned disks retain donor BCD GUIDs when CloneTool run with 'preserve-uuid' flag. Workaround tested: rebuild BCD store with bcdboot and regenerate machine IDs allows provisioning to proceed. Need to validate automation-safe approach.

2026-03-11 Lina Patel (Security): Flagging potential inventory mismatch risk — duplicate hardware IDs could confuse asset DB and EDR correlation. Recommend blocking 'preserve-uuid' cloning for corporate devices.

2026-03-12 Diego Ramos: Submitted quick fix PR to provisioner repo to detect duplicate BCD GUIDs (hook that runs 'bcdedit /enum' and regenerates if collision detected). PR referenced above; testing in lab continues.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Disk-clone process preserved donor BCD store including GUID elements used by Windows/Intune to correlate machine identity. When the cloned device attempts registration, Intune/Windows setup treats the GUID as a device identifier conflict and aborts join. Confirmed by matching GUIDs between donor and failed device. Intervention: regenerate BCD store and run sysprep-like identity refresh. Risk: naive regeneration may break secure boot or BitLocker bindings — validate with encrypted devices in a safe test set.
resolution:
Mitigation: Temporary depot screen-instructions added: after SSD clone, run 'bcdboot C:\Windows' to recreate BCD store and then run 'sysprep /generalize' in offline image rebuild flow; this allows devices to complete AAD join. Proposed long-term fix: update depot cloning SOP to disable UUID-preserve option and add a pre-provision hook in provisioner to detect and refresh duplicate BCD entries.

Follow-ups: 1) Update Depot Runbook (Confluence) — assigned to Diego. 2) Enforce clone-tool configuration change across depot fleet — operations ticket to be raised. 3) Run audit of recently repaired devices in last 30 days to find any other collisions.
next_steps: 1) Finish automated detection + regeneration PR testing and merge if green. 2) Deploy provisioner change to lab-staging, monitor for regressions. 3) Update depot SOP and communicate to hardware repair partners. 4) Run targeted lookup for duplicate BCD GUIDs in asset DB and remediate any matches.
workaround: Manual: On affected device boot to WinPE, run 'bcdedit /export C:\bcd_backup' then 'bcdboot C:\Windows' to recreate the BCD store. If BitLocker enabled, suspend protection first and re-protect after regeneration. After this, re-run provisioning and Azure AD join.
time_estimate_for_fix: 2 days for testing + 1 day for deploy and runbook updates
